claim: it is also the one DAC of the three with a white wine, from Grüner Veltliner, Weissburgunder, Chardonnay and Neuburger
because: The current Eisenberg DAC regulation lets the wines be made from Blaufränkisch 'oder Welschriesling (nur bei Angabe einer Ried)'. That means Eisenberg now also has a white DAC wine, a Welschriesling that must carry a Ried name, so Leithaberg is no longer the only one of the three with a white. The Welschriesling category came in with a later amendment to the Eisenberg rules; the original 2009 DAC was Blaufränkisch only.
fix: it is also the one DAC of the three with a full white category (Grüner Veltliner, Weissburgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger); Eisenberg now also allows a single-Ried Welschriesling
